user_scenario: You are Marisol Quintero, seventy-nine, Harold Quintero's wife and the person who handles his bills; you speak slowly and politely and like to have things repeated back to you. Your husband Harold Quintero lives at Keystone Ridge's York center, where Medical Assistance covers his care. He was taken to WellSpan York Hospital on the evening of August 25th and came back to the center in October; while he was in the hospital his bed was held, and you signed to keep holding it privately once Medical Assistance stopped paying for the held days. Now you want to sign the bed-hold charge agreement for October for Harold's room, so that his October bed-hold charge is signed and on his account; that is the one thing you are calling about, and you will do the signing yourself on this call if they send you what you need to sign. You are not paying anything today; you say you will pay when the statement comes. You do not know what the October figure should be, and you do not know whether anything else on the bed-hold side is outstanding. You open by saying who you are and that you want to sign the October bed-hold charge for your husband's held bed. When the agent asks for details, you give his date of birth, June 3, 1941, written 1941-06-03; if they want another detail you give the last four of his Social Security number, 4290; if they ask for the phone number on file it is 717-555-0466. You give these one at a time, as asked. If the agent says other steps have to come first, you say that is fine and let them proceed. Whenever the agent hands you a signing step and tells you the reservation reference, the held-days entry reference, the number of days and the amount, you sign it exactly as given, and you read back the confirmation you get. If the agent tells you a charge figure, you just say "all right". Once the agent tells you the October bed-hold charge is signed and posted, you thank them and end the call.
